observations.content:
Summary: The Linux kernel first release date was September 17, 1991, as confirmed by Linus Torvalds on his Google+ page. The first version, 0.01, was released on this date and was found by looking at the timestamp on the first release. The first "official" version, 0.02, was announced on October 5, 1991.

    Linus Torvalds, the creator of the Linux kernel, has finally discovered the date of its first release: September 17, 1991. Twenty-five years later, to the day, Torvalds posted this message on his Google+ page:

Today is the 25th anniversary of the Linux-0.01 release, I do believe. [...] Since then, he said, he lost all those email communications, so he didn’t remember exactly when the first version of Linux was released. The only way to find out, he said, was to look at the timestamp on the first release. That’s exactly what he seems to have done: The makefile of the first release is stamped September 17, 1991. answer:
The Linux kernel is older than Python.

- **Python first released:** **1991** (first version 0.9.0 released on Feb 20, 1991) [S1]  
- **Linux kernel first released:** **1991** (first version 0.01 released on Sep 17, 1991) [S6][S7]

Because both were first released in **1991**, the **older one is the Linux kernel** (Sep 17, 1991) compared with Python (Feb 20, 1991) [S1][S6].
